comparisons.peer_summary: AMD recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of the 2024 Restructuring Plan, which focused on driving efficiencies and aligning resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD disclosed significant restructuring charges in fiscal 2024 aimed at cost reduction and strategic alignment. Intel’s 2022 Restructuring Program, completed in Q1 2024, reduced its cost structure to allow reinvestment in resources and capacity (intc_2024_7_P084_S003, intc_2024_7_P084_S004). Similarly, AMD recognized $186 million in 2024 charges due to its 2024 Restructuring Plan, which focused on driving efficiencies and aligning resources with growth opportunities in AI and enterprise markets (amd_2024_7_P048_S001, amd_2024_7_P048_S002).

sentences.text: The charges in 2023 and 2022 primarily related to the 2022 Restructuring Program, which was approved to rebalance our workforce and operations in alignment with our strategy and was completed in Q1 2024.

The 2022 Restructuring Program, in conjunction with other initiatives, reduced our cost structure and allowed us to reinvest certain of these cost savings in resources and capacity to develop, manufacture, market, sell, and deliver our products in furtherance of our strategy.
We recognized $186 million of restructuring charges in 2024 due to the implementation of a restructuring plan (the 2024 Restructuring Plan).
The 2024 Restructuring Plan was focused on driving efficiencies across the business and aligning resources with our largest growth opportunities in the AI and enterprise markets.

comparisons.peer_summary: Restructuring and other charges recognized in operating expenses were $1,533 million in fiscal year 2024 and $244 million in fiscal year 2023. The 2024 charges primarily consisted of employee termination costs related to cost reduction activities associated with the VMware Merger, while the 2023 charges were primarily non-recurring charges related to IP litigation.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Broadcom reported restructuring charges in fiscal 2024 primarily driven by employee termination costs. Intel’s charges in 2023 and 2022 were related to the 2022 Restructuring Program, which was completed in Q1 2024 (intc_2024_7_P084_S003). Broadcom recognized $1,533 million in fiscal 2024, which primarily included employee termination costs from cost reduction activities related to the VMware Merger (avgo_2024_7_P052_S001, avgo_2024_7_P052_S002).

comparisons.peer_summary: In 2023, the company implemented cost reduction measures including a restructuring plan that reduced headcount by approximately 15%, incurred $171 million in restructure charges, and achieved estimated quarterly savings of $130 million through 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and Micron implemented restructuring plans that resulted in headcount reductions and cost savings, with impacts extending into 2024. Intel’s 2022 Restructuring Program, completed in Q1 2024, reduced its cost structure (intc_2024_7_P084_S003, intc_2024_7_P084_S004). Micron’s 2023 Restructure Plan substantially completed in 2023 reduced headcount by approximately 15% and yielded estimated quarterly cost savings of approximately $130 million subsequent to 2023 (mu_2024_7_P006_S004, mu_2024_7_P006_S006).

sentences.text: The charges in 2023 and 2022 primarily related to the 2022 Restructuring Program, which was approved to rebalance our workforce and operations in alignment with our strategy and was completed in Q1 2024.

The 2022 Restructuring Program, in conjunction with other initiatives, reduced our cost structure and allowed us to reinvest certain of these cost savings in resources and capacity to develop, manufacture, market, sell, and deliver our products in furtherance of our strategy.
Under the 2023 Restructure Plan, we reduced our headcount by approximately 15% by the end of calendar 2023, through a combination of voluntary attrition and personnel reductions.

The 2023 Restructure Plan, which was substantially completed in 2023, yielded estimated cost savings of approximately $130 million per quarter (approximately 60% in cost of goods sold, 30% in R&D, and 10% in SG&A) subsequent to 2023.
